title: Sentinel errors and when to declare one

videos.script: Lesson 34 found errors inside a chain, by value with errors.Is and by type with errors.As. This lesson is about the values worth finding, and who decides to make one. {{eof}} It starts with an error that is not a failure at all. io.EOF is how a reader says the input has ended. A loop that reads a string four bytes at a time meets it, and stops cleanly. {{store}} Then a sentinel of your own. A small store package declares ErrNotFound, wraps it with the item's name, and the program that calls it still recognises it. {{choose}} Last, the choice. Some errors deserve a variable, some deserve a type with fields, and most deserve neither. And a variable, once callers use it, is a promise. You will break that promise twice: once loudly, with a compile error, and once so quietly that nothing prints a word. By the end you can tell which kind of error a function should return, and what it costs to change your mind.
